sections.heading: C2 — Basic driving
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Basic driving

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A31
The handbook describes four steering methods for different vehicle-control tasks. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A31
Hand-to-hand steering is also called push-pull steering. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A31
For hand-to-hand steering, the left-hand starting position is between 7 and 8 o'clock. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A31
For hand-to-hand steering, the right-hand starting position is between 4 and 5 o'clock. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A31
In hand-to-hand steering, one hand pushes upward while the opposite hand slides up to grip and pull downward. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A31
As the pulling hand moves down during hand-to-hand steering, the hand that pushed slides toward its starting position. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A31
Reverse the hand-to-hand sequence to bring the vehicle back toward its intended path. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A31
Hand-to-hand steering keeps the hands and arms from crossing over the steering wheel. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A31
With a driver airbag, keeping the hands and arms from crossing the wheel reduces the chance of face, hand and arm injury in a frontal crash. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A31
The handbook identifies hand-to-hand steering as its preferred method. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A31
The handbook discourages the 2-and-10-o'clock position because of danger in airbag-equipped vehicles. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A31
Use hand-over-hand steering for low-speed turns, such as parking or turning at an intersection. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A31
For hand-over-hand steering, start the left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A31
For hand-over-hand steering, start the right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A31
During hand-over-hand steering to the right, work through the wheel's upper-right third. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A31
During hand-over-hand steering to the left, work through the wheel's upper-left third. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A31
Repeat the hand-over-hand sequence as needed to continue the turn. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A31
Reverse the hand-over-hand sequence to bring the vehicle back toward its intended path. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A31
When ABS is engaged and steering is needed to avoid a hazard, limiting steering input may be necessary to stay out of other lanes. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A31
After being forced off the road, limited steering input may be needed to avoid crossing into other lanes. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A31
At higher speeds, much less steering input is needed to move the vehicle one lane-width sideways. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A31
The handbook describes 45 to 90 degrees of steering for returning a modern vehicle to the road after leaving it. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A31
The handbook limits steering input during roadway evasion to no more than 180 degrees. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A31
The handbook warns that steering beyond 180 degrees during roadway evasion causes traction loss. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A31
Excessive steering during roadway evasion can carry the vehicle across the road toward oncoming traffic. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A31
Use one-hand steering only when backing or temporarily reaching for a vehicle control. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A31
When reaching for a control, keep the other hand in its normal operating position on the wheel. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A31
Depending on wheel design, the handbook places the steering hand at 8 to 9 o'clock or 3 to 4 o'clock during a temporary control reach. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A31
The handbook recommends the 12-o'clock position only when backing left or right and turning in the seat to see the rearward path. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A32
Minimize backing because seeing behind the vehicle is difficult. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R31 | anchor: A32
A drive-through parking space can allow a forward departure instead of backing out. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R32 | anchor: A32
Before getting into the vehicle, check behind it for children and small objects hidden from the driver's-seat view. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R33 | anchor: A32
For backing, hold the brake pedal while shifting into reverse. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R34 | anchor: A32
In the described backing procedure, hold the wheel at 12 o'clock with the left hand. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R35 | anchor: A32
In the described backing procedure, place the right arm on the seat back and look directly through the rear window. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R36 | anchor: A32
Rearview and side mirrors may be used while backing, but the handbook cautions that they do not show directly behind the vehicle. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R37 | anchor: A32
Back slowly with gentle, smooth acceleration. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R38 | anchor: A32
A vehicle is harder to steer while backing. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R39 | anchor: A32
When backing, make small steering movements toward the direction the rear should travel. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R40 | anchor: A32
When backing through a turn, make quick checks ahead and to the sides. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R41 | anchor: A32
Continue watching behind until the backing vehicle has stopped completely. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0032]

Misconceptions: Compare transmission and steering-method conditions in the fact blocks; do not transfer a condition to a different procedure.
Mnemonics: Editorial retrieval cue: prepare, observe, move, stop; the cue adds no driving rule.
Glossary: Use the sourced blocks to distinguish hand-to-hand, hand-over-hand, evasive and one-hand steering.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle-specific controls depend on the owner's manual; ambiguous instructions remain typed source debt rather than guessed equipment behavior.

ranked.label: Coverage of Basic driving; pedagogic emphasis only, no official exam weights asserted

corpus_stability.reason: The bound Kansas handbook has one February 2022 revision label; the selected source contains no evidence of multiple annual corpus rewrites. Later legal or administrative changes require issuer rechecking.

market_signal.origin_note: Market evidence is handled in part E.
